claim: In Italy, regions have the mandate to implement population-based screening programs for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer.
source: In Italy, regions have the mandate to implement population-based screening programs for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is a factual statement about Italian health policy.

claim: From March to May 2020, a severe lockdown was imposed due to the COVID-19 pandemic by the Italian Ministry of Health, with the suspension of screening programs.
source: From March to May 2020, a severe lockdown was imposed due to the COVID-19 pandemic by the Italian Ministry of Health, with the suspension of screening programs.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the timing and nature of the lockdown and its impact on screening programs.

claim: A reduction of subjects invited and tests performed, with differences between periods and geographical macro areas, was observed in 2020 vs. 2019.
source: A reduction of subjects invited and tests performed, with differences between periods and geographical macro areas, was observed in 2020 vs. 2019.
evidence: This claim is supported by the survey data comparing 2020 to 2019 activities.

claim: The reduction in examination coverage was larger than that in invitation coverage for all screening programs.
source: The reduction in examination coverage was larger than that in invitation coverage for all screening programs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data presented in the results.

claim: From the second half of 2020, the trend for test coverage showed a decrease in all the macro areas for all the screening programs.
source: From the second half of 2020, the trend for test coverage showed a decrease in all the macro areas for all the screening programs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by PASSI survey data.

claim: Compared with the pre-pandemic period, there was a greater difference according to the level of education in the odds of having had a test last year vs. never having been screened or not being up to date with screening tests.
source: Compared with the pre-pandemic period, there was a greater difference according to the level of education in the odds of having had a test last year vs. never having been screened or not being up to date with screening tests.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Poisson regression models in the results.

claim: The lockdown and the ongoing COVID-19 emergency caused an important delay in screening activities.
source: The lockdown and the ongoing COVID-19 emergency caused an important delay in screening activities.
evidence: This is stated in the conclusions and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The pandemic increased the preexisting individual and geographical inequalities in access to screening.
source: This increased the preexisting individual and geographical inequalities in access.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing differential impacts by education level and geography.

claim: The opportunistic screening did not mitigate the impact of the pandemic.
source: The opportunistic screening did not mitigate the impact of the pandemic.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and conclusions, supported by PASSI data showing no compensatory increase in opportunistic screening.

claim: The COVID-19 pandemic and control measures had an impact on all health services and on people's behaviors and attitudes toward prevention.
source: Since early 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic and the measures taken by most governments to control the spread of the virus had an impact on all health services, but also on people's behaviors and attitudes toward prevention (Kumari et al., 2021; Moynihan et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: The combination of reduced health service delivery for non-COVID-19 activities and a lower propensity to access health services by the population caused appreciable delays in cancer diagnosis in most countries.
source: The combination of reduced health service delivery for non-COVID-19 activities and a lower propensity to access health services by the population caused appreciable delays in cancer diagnosis in most countries where the phenomenon has been studied (Ferrara et al., 2021; Dinmohamed et al., 2020; Nyante et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Cancer screening tests were among the first suspended activities during the first pandemic wave in most European countries.
source: Cancer screening tests are nonurgent services, and thus they were among the first suspended activities during the first pandemic wave in most European countries (Figueroa et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: Organized screening programs actively invite the target population, which allows accurate planning of workload.
source: On the other hand, organized screening programs actively invite the target population. The active invitation allows to accurately plan the workload, which represented an opportunity for organized screening programs to resume post-lockdown activities in a rational way according to accurate prioritization, aiming to minimize the impact of the pandemic on cancer diagnosis delays (Castanon et al., 2021, Campbell et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and describes a characteristic of organized screening programs.

claim: The presence of a structured and well-organized program has been recognized as a possible element favoring the resilience of health services to the pandemic disruption.
source: Thus, the presence of a structured and well-organized program has been recognized as a possible element favoring the resilience of health services to the pandemic disruption (Mangone et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: A national law included organized screening programs for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancers among the public health interventions that all the regions must carry out.
source: In Italy, a national law included organized screening programs for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancers among the public health interventions that all the regions must carry out (Decreto del Presidente del Consiglio dei Ministri, 12 gennaio, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Italian legislation.

claim: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the invitation coverage was almost complete for all screening programs in Central Italy, and for breast cancer in Northern Italy.
source: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the invitation coverage was almost complete for all screening programs in Central Italy, and for breast cancer in Northern Italy, while for colorectal cancer screening, there were still areas, especially in Southern Italy, where large parts of the target population were not actively invited.
evidence: This is a statement about pre-pandemic screening coverage based on historical data.

claim: For colorectal cancer screening, there were still areas, especially in Southern Italy, where large parts of the target population were not actively invited before the pandemic.
source: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the invitation coverage was almost complete for all screening programs in Central Italy, and for breast cancer in Northern Italy, while for colorectal cancer screening, there were still areas, especially in Southern Italy, where large parts of the target population were not actively invited.
evidence: This is a statement about pre-pandemic screening coverage based on historical data.

claim: There are large differences in participation in all three screening programs among regions, with the northern regions achieving higher participation rates than the southern ones.
source: There are large differences in participation in all three screening programs among regions, with the northern regions achieving higher participation rates than the southern ones.
evidence: This is a statement about pre-pandemic screening participation based on historical data.

claim: In 2010–13 in Italy, test coverage in the target population reaches 75, 80, and 48% for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancers, respectively.
source: In 2010–13 in Italy, test coverage in the target population that reaches 75, 80, and 48% for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancers, respectively.
evidence: This is a statement about historical test coverage based on data from a cited study.

claim: About one fourth, one third, and one sixth of the coverage is attributable to opportunistic testing for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening test coverage, respectively.
source: The contribution of opportunistic screening to coverage differed across the three screening programs with about one fourth, one third, and one sixth of the coverage attributable to opportunistic testing for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening test coverage, respectively (Carrozzi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In Italy, the first diagnosis of COVID-19 was made on February 20, 2020.
source: In Italy, the first diagnosis of COVID-19 was made on February 20, 2020, and a strict lockdown started on March 8 (Marziano et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timeline of COVID-19 in Italy, supported by a citation.

claim: A strict lockdown started on March 8, 2020 in Italy.
source: In Italy, the first diagnosis of COVID-19 was made on February 20, 2020, and a strict lockdown started on March 8 (Marziano et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timeline of COVID-19 in Italy, supported by a citation.

claim: The impact of the first wave in terms of deaths was very strong and concentrated in Northern Italy.
source: The impact of this first wave in terms of deaths was very strong and concentrated in Northern Italy.
evidence: This is supported by the mortality data presented in Figure 1.

claim: A second wave started in October and lasted until the end of the year, involving all the Italian regions.
source: A second wave started in October and lasted until the end of the year, involving all the Italian regions (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: From March to May, the lockdown stopped all nonessential activities.
source: Control measures differed in the three periods: from March to May, the lockdown stopped all nonessential activities; during the summer, almost all restrictions were removed; while during the October to December restrictions, school closures, limits to movement and recommendations to work from home were applied on a regional or even provincial basis according to incidence (Manica et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about control measures, supported by a citation.

claim: During the summer, almost all restrictions were removed.
source: Control measures differed in the three periods: from March to May, the lockdown stopped all nonessential activities; during the summer, almost all restrictions were removed; while during the October to December restrictions, school closures, limits to movement and recommendations to work from home were applied on a regional or even provincial basis according to incidence (Manica et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about control measures, supported by a citation.

claim: During October to December, school closures, limits to movement and recommendations to work from home were applied on a regional or even provincial basis according to incidence.
source: Control measures differed in the three periods: from March to May, the lockdown stopped all nonessential activities; during the summer, almost all restrictions were removed; while during the October to December restrictions, school closures, limits to movement and recommendations to work from home were applied on a regional or even provincial basis according to incidence (Manica et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about control measures, supported by a citation.

claim: Breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screenings are recommended in Italy, and regional health systems are in charge of implementing them according to the recommendations of the European Commission and of the Italian Ministry of Health.
source: In Italy, breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screenings are recommended, and regional health systems are in charge of implementing them according to the recommendations of the European Commission and of the Italian Ministry of Health.
evidence: This is a statement about the Italian health system structure and policy.

claim: After the first COVID-19 case was diagnosed on February 20, small clusters were identified and restrictions on movements in small areas in Northern Italy were set.
source: After the first COVID-19 case was diagnosed on February 20, apparently, small clusters were identified and restrictions on movements in small areas in Northern Italy were set.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the early response to COVID-19 in Italy.

claim: On March 9, the first lockdown measures were put in place for the whole country, causing the suspension of screening first-level activities.
source: On March 9, the first lockdown measures were put in place for the whole country, causing the suspension of screening first-level activities.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the lockdown and its impact on screening.

claim: National directives recommended maintaining diagnostic assessment in those who tested positive and assuring all oncological follow-up.
source: On the contrary, national directives recommended maintaining diagnostic assessment in those who tested positive and assuring all oncological follow-up (Decreto del Presidente del Consiglio dei Ministri del 9 marzo, 2020, Ministero della Salut, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to official directives.

claim: The strict lockdown ended at the beginning of May 2020.
source: The strict lockdown, that is, the 'stay at home' period in which only essential activities were allowed, ended at the beginning of May 2020, but the restrictions were gradually removed until the beginning of June 2020, when only physical distancing and wearing face masks remained mandatory (Marziano et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timeline of restrictions, supported by a citation.

claim: Restrictions were gradually removed until the beginning of June 2020, when only physical distancing and wearing face masks remained mandatory.
source: The strict lockdown, that is, the 'stay at home' period in which only essential activities were allowed, ended at the beginning of May 2020, but the restrictions were gradually removed until the beginning of June 2020, when only physical distancing and wearing face masks remained mandatory (Marziano et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timeline of restrictions, supported by a citation.

claim: During the summer, COVID-19 incidence remained relatively low throughout the country.
source: During the summer, COVID-19 incidence remained relatively low throughout the country, but in October it increased rapidly and new restrictions were introduced (Manica et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and the data in Figure 1.

claim: In October, COVID-19 incidence increased rapidly and new restrictions were introduced.
source: During the summer, COVID-19 incidence remained relatively low throughout the country, but in October it increased rapidly and new restrictions were introduced (Manica et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and the data in Figure 1.

claim: Regions or provinces were classified as white, yellow, orange, and red according to a set of indicators measuring the quality of data reporting, the testing capacity, the incidence trend (the Rt), the adequacy of contact tracing, and the pressure on the health system.
source: Regions or provinces were classified as white, yellow, orange, and red according to a set of indicators measuring the quality of data reporting, the testing capacity, the incidence trend (the Rt), the adequacy of contact tracing, and the pressure on the health system (Riccardo et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the classification system, supported by a citation.

claim: Each color code corresponded to a set of mandatory restrictions that the regional government should implement and eventually integrate with local measures.
source: Each color code corresponded to a set of mandatory restrictions that the regional government should implement and eventually integrate with local measures.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the restriction system.

claim: None of the measures were directed to reduce nonurgent health services.
source: Among these measures, none was directed to reduce nonurgent health services and, in several regions, cancer screening had been included among the services, which had to be maintained.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the official measures.

claim: In several regions, cancer screening had been included among the services which had to be maintained.
source: Among these measures, none was directed to reduce nonurgent health services and, in several regions, cancer screening had been included among the services, which had to be maintained.
evidence: This is a factual statement about regional policies.

claim: In many areas, the pressure on hospitals became so strong that it became necessary to reduce nonurgent activities in order to redirect health professionals to COVID-19-related activities.
source: Nevertheless, in many areas, the pressure on hospitals became so strong that it became necessary to reduce nonurgent activities in order to redirect health professionals to COVID-19-related activities.
evidence: This is a statement about what happened in practice despite official policies.

claim: In orange and red zones there were restrictions on moving from one municipality to another.
source: Furthermore, in orange and red zones there were restrictions on moving from one municipality to another (even if these did not apply for medical checks/reasons) and restrictions on public transport.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the restrictions in place.

claim: In total, 21 regions out of 21 participated in the ONS survey.
source: In total, 21 regions out of 21 participated in the survey.
evidence: This is a statement about the survey participation.

claim: With the first lockdown measures on March 9, 2020, all screening first-level activities should be suspended maintaining diagnostic assessment in those who tested already positive.
source: With the first lockdown measures on March 9, 2020, all screening first-level activities should be suspended maintaining diagnostic assessment in those who tested already positive.
evidence: This is a statement about the official directive.

claim: The suspension was heterogeneous across regions.
source: Qualitative data from the survey show that, regardless of national directives, the suspension was heterogeneous.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: The suspension was almost complete in most Northern and Central regions where screening invitations and test delivery were immediately suspended.
source: It was almost complete in most Northern and Central regions where screening invitations and test delivery were immediately suspended; in Lazio, the suspension was established late; while in other regions, according to the screening organization, test delivery was maintained for colorectal (Puglia, Umbria) and cervical (Valle D'Aosta) cancer campaigns.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: Assessment of people who had previously had a positive screening test was never stopped in any program.
source: Assessment of people who had previously had a positive screening test was never stopped in any program.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: Most screening programs started again in May/June.
source: Most screening programs started again in May/June, but rules to reduce the risk of infection required avoiding crowding in waiting rooms and physical distancing in the clinics, thus the number of exams per hour was reduced by 30–50% in all programs.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: Rules to reduce the risk of infection required avoiding crowding in waiting rooms and physical distancing in the clinics, thus the number of exams per hour was reduced by 30–50% in all programs.
source: Most screening programs started again in May/June, but rules to reduce the risk of infection required avoiding crowding in waiting rooms and physical distancing in the clinics, thus the number of exams per hour was reduced by 30–50% in all programs.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: These restrictions lasted for the entire study period.
source: These restrictions lasted for the entire study period.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: Many programs reported a reduction in the pace of invitations during the second wave of the pandemic in the autumn of 2020.
source: Furthermore, many programs reported a reduction in the pace of invitations during the second wave of the pandemic in the autumn of 2020.
evidence: This is based on qualitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: In 2020, the screening invitations decreased for cervical, breast, and colorectal cancer screening in Northern and Southern Italy, compared with those of the 2017–2019 period.
source: According to the quantitative survey, in 2020, the screening invitations decreased, for cervical, breast, and colorectal cancer screening in Northern and Southern Italy, compared with those of the 2017–2019 period.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey.

claim: Central Italy registered the best performances: cervical cancer screening programs were able to maintain invitation coverage close to 100% and breast and colorectal cancer screening resulted in just below 90%.
source: It is worth noting that Central Italy registered the best performances: cervical cancer screening programs were indeed able to maintain invitation coverage close to 100% and breast and colorectal cancer screening resulted in just below 90% (Figure 2).

claim: The reduction in invitations was large and consistent in all macro areas and all screening programs for the first (January to May 2020) and second (June to September 2020) periods.
source: The reduction in invitations was large and consistent in all macro areas and all screening programs for the first (January to May 2020) and second (June to September 2020) periods.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In the third period (October to December 2020), in Central Italy, programs tried to catch up with the backlog of invitations, while in Northern Italy the programs mostly continued with the pre-pandemic pace.
source: In the third one (October to December 2020), differences emerged: in Central Italy, programs tried to catch up with the backlog of invitations, while in Northern Italy the programs mostly continued with the pre-pandemic pace.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In Southern Italy, the reduction in activity remained up to the first quarter of 2021, except for colorectal cancer screening.
source: In Southern Italy, the reduction in activity remained up to the first quarter of 2021, except for colorectal cancer screening (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Compared to 2017–2019, in 2020 the reduction in examination coverage was larger than the reduction in invitation coverage for all screenings and in all macro areas.
source: Compared to 2017–2019, in 2020 the reduction in examination coverage was larger than the reduction in invitation coverage for all screenings and in all macro areas (Figure 1).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In Central and Northern Italy, the reduction in tests performed was particularly strong in the first period and then decreased gradually, reaching pre-pandemic levels for breast and colorectal cancer screening in the first quarter of 2021, but not for cervix cancer screening in Northern Italy.
source: In Central and Northern Italy, it was particularly strong in the first period and then decreased gradually (Figure 3), reaching pre-pandemic levels for breast and colorectal cancer screening in the first quarter of 2021, but not for cervix cancer screening in Northern Italy.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In Southern Italy, the reduction in tests performed lasted until the end of 2020 and it is still strong for cervical and breast cancer screening in the first quarter of 2021.
source: In Southern Italy, the reduction in tests performed lasted until the end of 2020 and it is still strong for cervical and breast cancer screening in the first quarter of 2021 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The delay accumulated until May 2021 in screening the target population differs by macro area, and it is larger for Southern Italy and smaller for Central Italy for the three programs.
source: The delay accumulated until May 2021 in screening the target population differs by macro area, and it is larger for Southern Italy and smaller for Central Italy for the three programs.
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Table 2.

claim: In Northern and Central Italy one or more regions cumulated a negligible delay of fewer than 45 days, while some regions cumulated about 1 year of delay in all programs.
source: In fact, in Northern and Central Italy one or more regions cumulated a negligible delay of fewer than 45 days, while some regions cumulated about 1 year of delay in all programs (Table 2).
evidence: This is based on quantitative data from the ONS survey and shown in Table 2.

claim: The trend for test coverage as reported by PASSI showed a clear decrease in all the macro areas for the mammographic and colorectal screenings starting from the second half of 2020.
source: The trend for test coverage as reported by PASSI showed a clear decrease in all the macro areas for the mammographic and colorectal screenings starting from the second half of 2020 (Figure 4).

claim: For coverage with Pap tests or HPV tests, the decrease is appreciable, but the magnitude is smaller.
source: Also, for coverage with Pap tests or HPV tests, the decrease is appreciable, but the magnitude is smaller.

claim: In 2020 there was an inversion in a long-term trend, with a decrease in opportunistic screening in favor of organized screening for cervical cancer.
source: It is also appreciable that in 2020 we had an inversion in a long-term trend, with a decrease in opportunistic screening in favor of organized screening for cervical cancer (Figure 5).

claim: The decrease in test coverage is steeper in people with a lower level of educational level or with many perceived economic difficulties.
source: The decrease in test coverage is steeper in people with a lower level of educational level or with many perceived economic difficulties (Figures 6 and 7).

claim: For cervical cancer, the proportion of women aged 25–64 years that declared to have a test in the last year decreased dramatically for the screening program and to a lesser extent for opportunistic tests.
source: For cervical cancer, the proportion of women aged 25–64 years that declared to have a test in the last year decreased dramatically for the screening program and to a lesser extent for opportunistic tests.
evidence: This is based on PASSI survey data and shown in Figure 8.

claim: For breast and colorectal cancer, the reduction in tests performed in the last year was smaller and all attributable to organized screening.
source: For breast and colorectal cancer, the reduction was smaller and all attributable to organized screening (Figure 8).
evidence: This is based on PASSI survey data and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The probability of having a test in the last year was lower in 2020 even when adjusting for all other variables.
source: Multivariate Poisson models show that the probability of having a test in the last year was lower even when adjusting for all other variables (Table 3).
evidence: This is based on Poisson regression models using PASSI data shown in Table 3.

claim: In 2020, the probability of having had a test in the last year showed larger differences according to the level of education than in the pre-pandemic period for the three screenings.
source: Furthermore, stratifying the Poisson models by period, in 2020, the probability of having had a test in the last year showed larger differences according to the level of education than in the pre-pandemic period for the three screenings (Table 4); nevertheless, the differences could be due to random fluctuations.

claim: In 2020, for breast cancer screening only foreigners had a lower probability of having had a test than Italians, inverting what was observed in the pre-pandemic period.
source: Furthermore, in 2020, for breast cancer screening only foreigners had a lower probability of having had a test than Italians, inverting what was observed in the pre-pandemic period (Table 3).
evidence: This is based on Poisson regression models using PASSI data shown in Table 3.

claim: The differences by age and economic difficulties remained substantially unchanged in the pandemic compared with the pre-pandemic period.
source: The differences by age and economic difficulties remained substantially unchanged in the pandemic compared with the pre-pandemic period.

source: Other studies reported an early disruption of screening activities following the lockdown, with invitations and first-level tests being stopped, and a reduction in participation when invitations restarted (Eijkelboom et al., 2021a; Peacock et al., 2021; Ho et al., 2022; Eijkelboom et al., 2021b; Bosch et al., 2022).

claim: The reported data show large differences across countries in the screening programs' ability to resume their activity and in catching up with the cumulated backlog.
source: The reported data show large differences across countries in the screening programs' ability to resume their activity and in catching up with the cumulated backlog.
evidence: This is an inference based on the literature cited.

claim: Italy has a federal health system in which the implementation of screening programs is delegated to the regional government and practically managed by the local health authorities.
source: Italy has a federal health system in which the implementation of screening programs is delegated to the regional government and practically managed by the local health authorities.
evidence: This is a statement about the Italian health system structure.

claim: This organizational model, together with historical differences in the robustness of screening programs and the population's trust in the public health system, resulted in an extreme variability in the delay cumulated in more than 1 year of COVID-19 emergency.
source: This organizational model, together with historical differences in the robustness of screening programs and the population's trust in the public health system, resulted in an extreme variability in the delay cumulated in more than 1 year of COVID-19 emergency (Giorgi Rossi et al., 2019).

claim: Some areas showed the ability to recover all the backlog, while the vast majority were still cumulating further delay in the first months of 2021.
source: In fact, some areas showed the ability to recover all the backlog, while the vast majority were still cumulating further delay in the first months of 2021.

claim: These differences increased the already existing geographical inequalities across the country.
source: These differences increased the already existing geographical inequalities across the country.

claim: The difference by educational level seems to be stronger in 2020 than in previous years.
source: In fact, the difference by educational level seems to be stronger in 2020 than in previous years.

claim: In breast cancer screening differences disadvantaging immigrants were small in previous years but became larger in 2020.
source: Furthermore, in breast cancer screening differences disadvantaging immigrants – that were small in previous years – became larger in 2020.

claim: Immigrants rely mostly on organized screening and scarcely on opportunistic screening for mammography, which is a relatively expensive test.
source: Even if this difference could be due to chance, it may also reflect that immigrants rely mostly on organized screening and scarcely on opportunistic screening for mammography, which is a relatively expensive test.

claim: A model assuming a 12-month suspension of screening and early diagnosis pathways in England estimated an excess of about 300 breast cancer deaths (8–10% increase) and 1500 colorectal cancer deaths (15–17%) in the next 5 years.
source: For breast and colorectal cancer, in England, a model assuming a 12-month suspension of screening and early diagnosis pathways and reallocating all diagnoses to symptomatic diagnosis estimated an excess of about 300 breast cancer deaths (8–10% increase) and 1500 colorectal cancer deaths (15–17%) in the next 5 years (Maringe et al., 2020).

claim: The expected health impact of the disruption may be larger for clinical than for screening services.
source: The expected health impact of the disruption may be larger for clinical than for screening services.

source: The results of simulation models focused on the analysis of the impact of screening programs disruption are suggesting that we can expect a relative increase in breast and colorectal cancer-specific mortality ranging between 1% and 3% over the next 10–30 years, depending on the duration of the disruption and on the catch-up strategies adopted.
evidence: This is based on simulation models from the literature.

claim: More than half of the excess deaths are expected to occur during the first 5–10 years following disruption and the health impact might be larger for older people and disadvantaged population subgroups.
source: More than half of the excess deaths are expected to occur during the first 5–10 years following disruption and the health impact might be larger for older people and disadvantaged population subgroups.

claim: We can expect a similar impact of screening disruption in Italy, where we observed a wide variability in the length of disruption, with a 6-month average delay in the invitations.

evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the Italian data and modeling literature.

claim: Catch-up of backlog was different across regions, and differences cannot be explained by the severity of the pandemic in different areas.
